title: Hace... Que Expressions
description: Master the hace + time + que construction for talking about duration and time in the past.

grammar.title: Desde Hace vs. Hace
grammar.content:
Both 'desde hace' and 'hace... que' express duration:

DESDE HACE + time (verb in present or past):
Vivo aqui desde hace cinco anos. (I have lived here for five years.)
Estaba aqui desde hace dos horas. (He had been here for two hours.)

HACE + time + QUE + verb:
Hace cinco anos que vivo aqui. (I have lived here for five years.)

Negative with hace... que:

Hace anos que no la veo. (I haven't seen her for years.)
Hace mucho que no llueve. (It hasn't rained in a long time.)

With states (ser/estar):
Hace anos que es doctor. (He has been a doctor for years.)
Hace meses que esta enfermo. (He has been sick for months.)
examples: Cuanto tiempo hace que trabajas aqui? (How long have you been working here?)
Hace anos que no veo a Juan. (I haven't seen Juan in years.)
Estoy aqui desde hace una hora. (I have been here for an hour.)

grammar.title: Hace... Que vs. Hizo... Que
grammar.content:
HACE... QUE (imperfect/progressive) = how long (ongoing)
HIZO... QUE (preterite) = how long ago (completed)

Ongoing (imperfect):
Hace dos horas que te esperaba. (I had been waiting for you for two hours.) — past ongoing

Completed (preterite):
Hizo dos horas que te espere. (It was two hours ago that I waited for you.) — completed

Most common use: present perfect with 'hace'

PRESENT PERFECT with hace... que:

Hace + time + que + present perfect

Hace tres dias que llegue. (I arrived three days ago.)
Hace una semana que compre este coche. (I bought this car a week ago.)

Note: This is PRESENT PERFECT, not preterite. The action happened in the past but we're measuring from now.
examples: Hace tres dias que llegué. (I arrived three days ago.)
Hace un mes que empecé a trabajar. (I started working a month ago.)
Cuanto tiempo hace que lo conoces? (How long have you known him?)

grammar.title: Hace... Que — Duration in the Past
grammar.content:
HACE... QUE tells how long something has been going on:

Hace + time + que + verb in past

Hace dos anos que vive aqui. (He has been living here for two years.)
Hace tres meses que estudio espanol. (I have been studying Spanish for three months.)

Alternative: Verb in present + desde hace + time

Vivo aqui desde hace dos anos. (I have been living here for two years.)
Estudio desde hace tres meses. (I have been studying for three months.)

Both structures are interchangeable:
Hace un ano que trabajo aqui. = Trabajo aqui desde hace un ano.

For questions:
Cuanto tiempo hace que...? (How long has it been that...?)
Cuanto tiempo hace que vive aqui? (How long has he been living here?)
examples: Hace cinco anos que soy professor. (I have been a professor for five years.)
Hace dos horas que espero. (I have been waiting for two hours.)
Cuanto tiempo hace que la conoces? (How long have you known her?)
Trabajo aqui desde hace tres meses. (I have been working here for three months.)

grammar.title: Present Subjunctive in Fixed Expressions
grammar.content:
The subjunctive (subjuntivo) is a mood used to express wishes, doubts, emotions, and hypothetical situations. At A2.1, you'll mainly encounter it in fixed expressions — set phrases where the subjunctive is mandatory.

Wishes and blessings:
- ¡Que tengas un buen día! = Have a good day!
- ¡Que te vaya bien! = Good luck! (literally: may it go well for you)
- ¡Que descanses! = Rest well!

With querer/esperar + que (when the subject changes):
- Quiero que seas feliz. = I want you to be happy.
- Espero que llueva. = I hope it rains.

Common fixed expressions:
- Ojalá (que)... = I hope that... / God willing...
- Es importante que... = It's important that...
- Mejor que... = Better if...

The present subjunctive yo form is built by taking the yo present indicative form and switching the ending: -o → -e for -AR, -o → -a for -ER/-IR:
- hablar → hablo → hable
- comer → como → coma
- vivir → vivo → viva
examples: ¡Que tengas un excelente día! (Have an excellent day!)
Ojalá llueva mañana. (I hope it rains tomorrow.)
Quiero que tú vengas a mi fiesta. (I want you to come to my party.)
Espero que esté bien. (I hope he/she is okay.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian uses a similar 'optative' mood for wishes: 'Să ai o zi bună!' = '¡Que tengas un buen día!' The 'să' particle marks the subjunctive optative. This makes the Spanish subjunctive much more natural for Romanian speakers than for English speakers.

pronunciation.title: Hace Que Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
hace = AH-seh (sounds like 'ass-eh')
que = keh

Common phrases:

hace un momento = AH-seh oon moh-MEN-toh (a moment ago)
hace poco = AH-seh POH-koh (a little while ago)
hace tiempo = AH-seh TYEM-poh (some time ago)
hace mucho = AH-seh MOO-choh (a long time ago)

When hace starts a question:
Cuanto tiempo hace que...? = KWAN-toh TYEM-poh AH-seh keh...
(Cuanto sounds like 'kwahn-toh')
examples: Hace dos anos. = AH-seh dhes AH-nyohs
Hace tres meses que estudio. = AH-seh tres MEH-sehs keh es-TOO-dyoh
Cuanto tiempo hace que lo conoces? = KWAN-toh TYEM-poh AH-seh keh loh koh-NEH-sehs

exercises.question: How do you say 'I have been studying for three months' in Spanish?
options: Both A and C are correct
exercises.explanation: Both 'Hace tres meses que estudio' and 'Estudio desde hace tres meses' are correct.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ tres dias que llegue. (I arrived three days ago.)'
exercises.explanation: Hace + time + que + present perfect = time ago. 'Hace tres dias que llegue' = I arrived three days ago.

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'How long have you been living here?'
options: Cuanto tiempo hace que vives aqui?
Cuanto tiempo hace que vivias aqui?
exercises.explanation: 'Cuanto tiempo hace que vives aqui?' uses present tense for ongoing action.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Vivo aqui ___ hace cinco anos. (I have been living here for five years.)'
exercises.explanation: Desde hace = for (duration). 'Vivo aqui desde hace cinco anos' = I have been living here for five years.

exercises.question: How do you say 'I haven't seen her for years' in Spanish?
options: Hace anos que no la veo
Tengo anos que no la veo
exercises.explanation: Negative: 'Hace anos que no la veo' = I haven't seen her for years.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ tiempo hace que lo conoces? (How long have you known him?)'
exercises.explanation: Cuanto tiempo hace que...? = How long has it been that...? / How long have you...?

exercises.question: Which is correct: 'I have been waiting for two hours'?
exercises.explanation: Both 'Hace dos horas que espero' and 'Espero desde hace dos horas' are correct.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ mucho que no llueve. (It hasn't rained in a long time.)'
exercises.explanation: Hace mucho que no + verb = hasn't done something in a long time.

exercises.question: Which tense is used with 'hace... que' for ongoing actions in present?
exercises.explanation: Present tense is used with 'hace... que' for ongoing actions in present: 'Hace tres horas que trabajo'.

exercises.question: Complete: ' ___ dos horas que te ___ esperando. (I had been waiting for you for two hours.)'
exercises.explanation: Past ongoing uses imperfect: 'Hace dos horas que te estaba esperando' = I had been waiting for you.
